## Hook (first 3 seconds)
**On-screen text:** "18 hours for one cup of coffee."
**Visual:** Tight shot of cold water dripping into a jar of coffee grounds, timer in corner reading 00:00. First frame reads the same muted.
**VO:** "Eighteen hours for one cup of coffee. Here's why we don't rush it."

*Hook archetype: Specific number. Structure: Hook / Proof / Payoff / One ask.*

## Body (3-4 scenes with cues)

**Scene 1 — The problem (≈4s)**
**On-screen text:** "Heat = speed. Heat = bitterness."
**Visual:** Split frame — steaming hot-brew mug on the left, cold jar on the right.
**VO:** "Hot water pulls the flavour out fast — and the bitter stuff with it."

**Scene 2 — The mechanism (≈5s)**
**On-screen text:** "Cold water skips the bitter compounds."
**Visual:** Slow-motion grounds blooming in cold water; timer ticking up.
**VO:** "Cold water moves slower, so it leaves the harsh acids and oils behind. That's the whole trick."

**Scene 3 — Why 18 specifically (≈4s)**
**On-screen text:** "Less than 18h = weak. More = flat."
**Visual:** Three jars side by side labelled 12h, 18h, 24h; hand lifts the 18h jar.
**VO:** "Under eighteen hours it's thin. Over, it goes flat. Eighteen is the sweet spot."

**Scene 4 — Payoff (≈4s)**
**On-screen text:** "Smooth. Never bitter."
**Visual:** The finished pour over ice, condensation on the glass, first sip.
**VO:** "That's why ours tastes smooth all the way down — no bitterness to hide."

## CTA
**On-screen text:** "Send this to the friend who still drinks it bitter."
**Visual:** Cut back to the full glass — loops cleanly into the opening jar shot.
**VO:** "Send this to someone who thinks cold brew has to be bitter."
